newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LEV RISES TO 1.435-1,445 TO DLR AT CLOSE.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LEV RISES TO 1.435-1,445 TO DLR AT CLOSE.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed at 1,435-1,445 per dollar, up from the morning's 1,485-1,500 and 1,475-1,485 at the previous close as dollar supply heavily topped demand, dealers said.
"The lev gained some 50 (levs) against the dollar from the morning because of aggressive foreign currency selling while demand was very low", a commercial bank dealer said.
Local and foreign investors were selling foreign currency for levs to buy high-yield government securities, encouraged by the recent lev rise, dealers said.
The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) was not seen buying dollars today to halt the lev rise, dealers said.
"It is natural for the BNB to refrain from supporting the dollar amid expectations of a cut in the main interest rate, which might increase pressure on the lev," another dealer said.

The BNB was expected to cut today its main interest rate, now set at 8.03 percent monthly, in line with the falling effective monthly yield of seven- and 28-day discount T-bills sold daily at primary auctions.
The BNB said last week that it would adjust the main rate to the weighted average effective monthly yield of the seven- and 28-day T-bills auctioned daily by the Finance ministry.
Until last week the BNB calculated the main rate on the basis on the weighted average effective monthly yield of seven-day discount T-bills alone.
The average effective monthly yield on seven- and 28-day discount T-bills this week fell to 5.56-6.95 percent from 6.50-10.88 last week.
The weighted average effective monthly yield on 28-day discount T-bills was 5.78-6.85 percent this week. -- Sofia Newsroom, 3592 911 88
